title: King Manuel II to Queen Amélie, three code telegrams from Bussaco, August 1910 (ANTT PT/TT/CAM/M13; catalogue 408): transcribed, not read

steps.what: All 22 images of M13 fetched through the DigitArq JSON backend. Telegram forms on m0015, m0017, m0019, m0021, m0022 (three telegrams: m0015+m0017, m0019, m0021+m0022).
Transcribed the three telegrams with headers and stamps: 36, 3 and 54 items; the word counts on the forms (54, 72) match.

Repeats and shared groups: m0015 and m0021 share 37708, 39644, 93608, 97183 and open with a parallel run; m0019 repeats three groups of m0022. Random telegrams of the same sizes share two groups in about 1 of 10,000 trials.

Tried Sabugosa's 52 code values (targets/sabugosa1910) on the 79 five-digit groups, as written and with the struck third digit dropped: no match, and 7 groups would fall above the last known value (veio 9019). Not the same code in that form.
Looked through the clear letters of M13 for a decode: none for these telegrams.

outcome.method_basis: No decode of the time and no codebook; the groups are transcribed and the repeats listed.
outcome.fraction_read_source: documents[].length: 0 of 93 items have a value.

credits.note: attempt recorded: telegrams transcribed and analysed (repeats, shared groups, Sabugosa's code tried); no reading
three telegrams, 93 items, from the DigitArq images
dates and route: Bussaco -> Pena, 2 and 8 Aug 1910 (the catalogue gives 1908-1910)

gaps.item: all 93 items of the three telegrams
gaps.detail: no decode in M13 and no codebook found; the shared opening run is a possible crib only if a decode turns up

outcome.notes: Contributed by WAINUT (catalogue 408). The catalogue's 'some in cipher' concerns only the three telegrams; the letters of M13 are in clear.

prior.where: No decode in M13; no printed decipherment found (one web search by the first pass). M13 m0001-m0002 hold a pencil text in telegram style signed Manuel (London, a dinner given by the Queen Mother), which may be the decode of a telegram not in the file; it does not match these three.

human: WAINUT chose the catalogue items and set the rules; AI language-model agents fetched the images and transcribed them. No hand correction recorded.
